summary: A Quote subscription on an NSE equity made before Firstock has answered the login: the subscribe goes out at once (audit FB-01), then a V1 full tick and a V1 partial tick merged over it become Quote frames; after the unsubscribe a tick still in flight reaches nobody.

notes: Prices are paise; both divide by 100. The partial tick's zero open price never overwrites the snapshot, on the web (firstock_adapter.py:655-680) and the desktop (brokers/firstock/streaming.rs merge).

Audit FB-01, still open: FirstockFeed does not wait for the login answer (no awaits_auth_ack), so the subscribe frame reaches Firstock before {"status":"success"}; the web queues it until that answer (firstock_websocket.py:498-505, _process_pending_subscriptions). web.json cannot show the order of upstream frames, so the script's upstream_receives before the login push is the evidence.

deviations.reason: The web's Firstock adapter puts its mode number in data.mode (1, 2, 3); the desktop sends its label. data.mode follows each broker's web adapter (lead rule 2026-11-09): closed by the per-broker dialect switch.

Firstock's i_last_trade_time is in epoch seconds and the web sends it unchanged as ltt; feed timestamps are epoch milliseconds (docs/prompt/websockets-format.md). The desktop sends the trade time in ms.

The web's Quote sends oi 0 for an equity whose tick carries no open interest (data.get("i_open_interest", 0)); a value the broker did not send is left out, never sent as 0 (docs/api/websocket-streaming/quote.md, web openalgo#2376). The desktop's Quote leaves it out.
The web sends Firstock's circuit limits (i_upper_circuit_limit, i_lower_circuit_limit, /100); the desktop's common carrier drops them.
